newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rebound, led by technology rally.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rebound, led by technology rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks surged Friday as investors once again poured money into technology shares.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 61.58 points to 6,504.07, led by a solid rally from International Business Machines Corp.
In the broader market, gainers outpaced losers by eight to three on volume of 277 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite was up 19.20 points to 1,299.90, after earlier soaring 21 points to stand above 1,300 for the first time since Dec. 20.
"Some positive comments on Intel got the ball rolling and the other techs have followed suit," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management.
Intel Corp. was the most active issue on Nasdaq, surging 4-5/8 to 135 after Salomon Brothers strongly recommended buying the stock, upgrading it from hold.
Merrill Lynch also made bullish comments about the outlook for the U.S. semiconductor industry and said major firms in the group, such as Intel, could produce surprisingly strong earnings this year.
Also helping stocks was a reassuringly firm tone in the bond market, where interest rates had spiked higher over the last two sessions because of some surprisingly strong economic indicators.
"The bond market has started to stabilise and that's probably the principal reason stocks are staging such a strong recovery," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.

The benchmark 30-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.72 percent, versus 6.74 percent at Thursday's close, despite a report that showed U.S. construction spending rose a higher-than-expected 1.9 percent in November.
Earlier in the week, surprisingly strong home sales and manufacturing data triggered sharp declines in bond prices that in turn applied broad pressure to stock prices.
"The fact that the bond market could shake off the report suggests that maybe it's reached a level where bonds are starting to attract buyers," Johnson said.
Among the Dow industrials, the top gainers were IBM, which rose 3-3/8 to 156-5/8, and United Technologies Corp., up 2-1/8 to 67-3/4.

However, Filenet Corp. tumbled 8-1/8 to 23-5/8 after warning late Thursday that its fourth-quarter earnings would be hurt by customer order delays. The company said it expects to earn 20 cents per share in its fourth quarter, down from 32 cents a year ago.

State Street Boston Corp. jumped 7-1/4 to 70-1/8 on takeover speculation set off by news that Bank of New York Corp. was seeking approval to increase its stake in the company. Bank of New York rose 5/8 to 33-7/8.
CyberCash Inc. fell 4-1/4 to 19. Hambrecht & Quist downgraded the shares to hold from buy.
